taxonomy.subtopic: Intimal tear, false lumen, and dynamic branch-vessel obstruction

questions.stem_html:
A 52-year-old man with tall stature, pectus deformity, and a family history of sudden death develops abrupt chest pain while lifting a heavy box. The pain reaches maximal intensity immediately and radiates between the scapulae. Blood pressure is 178/92 mm Hg in the right arm and 142/78 mm Hg in the left. A new early diastolic murmur is present. CT angiography demonstrates a flap beginning in the ascending aorta and extending into the arch; the right renal artery intermittently fills from a compressed true lumen.

Which mechanism best explains the episodic reduction in right renal perfusion?

options.text_html: Motion of the intimal flap narrowing the branch-vessel origin during the cardiac cycle
Cholesterol crystal embolization from a stable infrarenal plaque
Diffuse renal arteriolar vasospasm caused by circulating catecholamines
Thrombosis of the renal vasa vasorum
Coronary steal through an aortocameral fistula

questions.explanation_html: An intimal tear allows blood to split the media and create a false lumen. The flap can prolapse across a branch ostium or compress the true lumen, producing dynamic malperfusion. Dynamic malperfusion in dissection is caused by pressure and motion of the false lumen and intimal flap, which can intermittently narrow the true lumen or a branch ostium.

wrong_choice_explanations.2: Cholesterol emboli usually follow vascular instrumentation and produce fixed small-vessel ischemia rather than beat-to-beat branch obstruction.
wrong_choice_explanations.3: Catecholamine vasoconstriction is systemic and does not explain a branch arising beside a dissection flap.
wrong_choice_explanations.4: Vasa vasorum injury weakens the aortic media but does not dynamically occlude the renal artery lumen.
wrong_choice_explanations.5: Coronary steal affects myocardial perfusion and is unrelated to renal branch malperfusion.

questions.educational_objective: Recognize that acute aortic dissection can cause organ ischemia through dynamic obstruction by an intimal flap, even without a fixed thrombus in the affected branch artery.
